By Chris De Silva

By Andrew McGarry

Topic:AFL

Taylor Walker kicked two vital goals in a downpour to help the Adelaide Crows beat Richmond at Adelaide Oval. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Sarah Reed)

After the ugliest of wins, Adelaide coach Matthew Nicks and his players had a collective wry grin.

"There were some smiles at the end, when you actually realise you get four points for that performance," he said.

Nicks acknowledged Adelaide's slogging nine-point victory over cellar dwellers Richmond — 9.9 (63) to 7.12 (54) — was ugly.

"If you play that way and win, maybe it's a good sign," he said after the rain-marred Adelaide Oval fixture.

"That even when we're nowhere near our best — and that was ugly tonight, unfortunately — and yet we still got the job done.

"There will be some guys that are challenged out of this one. And we'll learn from that and get better."

The Crows will simply have to be better to make any inroads in their upcoming finals campaign, let alone their next task: taking on ladder-leaders Fremantle in Perth on Friday night.

"We have got a short break into Freo," Nicks said.

"And there will be some changes to our side, everything going well."

Adelaide forward Darcy Fogarty has served his three-game suspension and first-choice ruckman Lachlan McAndrew will return from a rest.

Key defender James Borlase will be available after a hamstring scare and utility Luke Nankervis should return from a chest injury.

But the fifth-placed Crows, on 56 premiership points, blew a chance for a significant win that would have taken fourth spot from Brisbane — they trail the Lions by 0.2 per cent.

Nicks rejected any suggestion his team suffered from an attitude problem against the 17th-placed Tigers.

"It's not an attitude, it's never an attitude thing — that is not out group," he said.

"People have got it a little bit wrong: the competition is not that uneven.

"There are talented players on every team in the comp.

"There are some that have got a little more experience than others, and and a little bit more talent here and there.

"It was always going to be a tough game."

Port Adelaide star Jason Horne-Francis gave his team a big injury scare when he limped off in the final quarter against Sydney. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Jason McCawley)

Meanwhile, Jason Horne-Francis hobbled off the field in Port's 97-point loss to Sydney, as Geelong made light work of Essendon, triumphing by 67 points at Kardinia Park.

Earlier on Saturday, a huge final quarter from Harrison Petty helped Melbourne claim a four-point win over the AFL's ladder-leaders Fremantle.

Petty kicked 3.2 for the afternoon, including two in the final quarter as Melbourne emerged 17.11 (113) to 17.7 (109) winners in one of the games of the season at the MCG.

Prior to the action on Saturday, AFL boss Andrew Dillon addressed Geelong's concussion saga, ending a couple of days of silence from the league.

Look back at how the action unfolded in our live blog.

By Andrew McGarry

That's all we have for you tonight after some very interesting contests.

Melbourne's win over Fremantle gives impetus to the Demons' finals charge, and raises slight queries over the Dockers at the MCG. Not much, since they still lead the ladder by two games, but still.

The Swans win makes them hot, hot favourites for second spot, but the headline there is the injury to Jason Horne-Francis. We hope the scans are good news over the next 24-48 hours.

And although there were moments for both the Bombers and Tigers, once again they were not able to get over the line - the Tigers were a lot closer to victory than Essendon - as the narrow margin in Adelaide leaves the Crows needing everything to go their way for top-four.

We'll be back tomorrow with the final three games, starting with GWS vs Gold Coast in Sydney, followed by West Coast and Collingwood in Perth and then the round 22 finale - St Kilda vs Carlton at Docklands.

That last game will be a double-header with the start of the AFLW season, and the all-conquering North Melbourne will begin their flag defence against Geelong.

We'll see you then, but for now this is Andrew McGarry on behalf of Chris De Silva and Henry Hanson thanking you for joining us and wishing you a very good night.

Key Event

By Andrew McGarry

A relieved Matthew Nicks has spoken to Fox Footy after that win.

Asked about Izak Rankine's game, he replied: "It's a good thing he played, eh? That's going to be an ugly review for us (of that game).

"Not him (Rankine). That's what happens when you get the best players in the comp. He did it."

Asked about the three quarter time huddle and what he said to the players, he jokingly replied: "I blacked out!"

"I challenged them about what they want to be.

"We played our way to an ugly win.

"We move into an elimination final week (against Fremantle).

"Tonight we're in a good spot. We're disappointed in how we played. But you do what you (have to) do to win."

By Andrew McGarry

The Crows have to back up next Friday night in the west against the Fremantle Dockers - and THAT will be a huge contest.

Then they finish off at home at Adelaide Oval against GWS.

As we've said a few times tonight, there's not a lot of wiggle room for anyone, and the Crows perhaps more than most.

Key Event

By Andrew McGarry

Here's the ladder after a big day of footy, and the headline is the gap between the Lions in fourth and the Crows in fifth.

It's 0.2 percentage points. Not a whole lot of wiggle room for anyone in there right now.

By Andrew McGarry

That was a heart-stopping game for the Crows, and one of the reasons they got over the line was Izak Rankine.

He had 37 disposals, six marks, six tackles, 12 clearances, five score involvements, a whopping 19 contested possessions, 791 metres gained and THIS goal...

According to Fox Footy Rankine's performance was the highest-ranked game by an individual Crow in club history, surpassing the big Roo, Mark Ricciuto. Bravo, Izak.

Key Event

By Andrew McGarry

The siren sounds and the Crows breathe a sigh of relief!

They get the win by nine points, but it hasn't been impressive.

They also fail to get the percentage boost they needed. But they're still in it. Good grief, what a game!

By Andrew McGarry

Nathan Broad has had a ping from 50 in the last 90 seconds, and it has been punched through.

The Crows lead by nine points, and that should really be that.

But then again...

By Andrew McGarry

It's a really tense finish here, the Crows burst clear and Riley thilthorpe's kick for goal was chopped off by Nick Vlastuin.

But his kick out went to the Crows!

Zac Taylor marked ... and his kick swung through from 50 in the monsoon!

That's a 10-point lead to Adelaide.

By Andrew McGarry

We have five minutes to go, it's still an open-air shower stall, and the Tigers are attacking.

tom Brown runs onto it in the right forward pocket and snaps ... a point!

Four points in it.

By Andrew McGarry

Whoever comes out the wrong side of this one will be looking like this when the siren goes.

By Andrew McGarry

The tension is rising, and tempers are fraying at Adelaide Oval.

James Peatling gave away a free with a rough hit on Jack Ross.

Ross didn't like it, and slammed Peatling to the ground and had the free reversed!

This is getting spicy. half of the final term left. Five points.

By Andrew McGarry

This is like playing a game of footy in a (big) shower cubicle...

The rain is incessant, the players and the ball are sodden, and Richmond give away a 50.

Jordan Dawson has a kick for goal - and HE misses!

It's five points the margin.

By Andrew McGarry

Suddenly the Tigers are attacking, sensing a chance of a huge upset.

They are going down the right, and it's Seth Campbell (danger, danger Crows!).

He kicks on the run from the pocket, and could it go in? No, Sam Lalor marks it near the square!

But he misses the kick! It's four points the lead!

By Andrew McGarry

IS THAT THE GOAL OF THE NIGHT?

The Tigers are struggling to make ground, but a good kick down the wing finds Hugo Ralphsmith deep, deep in the right forward pocket.

It's hosing down, and Ralphsmith had a very difficult angle.

He went the checkside! It sailed through and the Crows fans are quiet. There are five points in it.

By Andrew McGarry

The Crows are looking surer with the ball in these horrible conditions. They go forward down the left, and Ben Keays kicks a speculator from near the boundary outside 50.

It bounces, bounces and is rushed through as another Crow is a metre behind the Tigers defender.

Plenty of time left, 11 points the margin. It's going to be VERY difficult to kick goals in this, you'd reckon.

By Andrew McGarry

A big start to the final quarter for the Crows!

Adelaide goes forward in the first minute and a bit, and the ball is in contest near the boundary on the wing. And it's 50!

Tex Walker did the big don't-argue on Kye Annand, and Annand got pinged for trying to get him again. Walker kicks the goal from 20m or so in front.

The Crows lead by 10 as the rain hoses down!

That's a big moment.

By Andrew McGarry

Any of our Commonwealth Games swimmers on the bench Andrew?

- Phillip

Phillip,

I don't think there are any swimmers there - but I reckon the coaches would bite your hand off to grab one if there were!

Key Event

By Andrew McGarry

The siren sounds, and it's going to be a nervous old finish at Adelaide Oval!

The Crows fans are up and about, with Izak Rankine in the final minutes reminding everyone why he's a star, booting a goal from just inside 50 in the wet to produce a massive roar from the stands.

Then a free kick to Callum Ah Chee for contact in a contest, and the former Lion slotted it to give the home side the lead!

Judson Clarke had a chance to put the Tigers back in front, but his kick on the run went wide in the last 60 seconds.

And with the last chance of the term, Tex Walker nearly, NEARLY took a grab in the goalsquare but couldn't hang on. Whew.

We are in a throwback game here, with 13 goals total to three quarter time.

So the news is good for the Crows, but not great - the home side's top-four hopes are on the line, but this is still a bit of a coin flip.

By Andrew McGarry

The weather is not fit for man nor beast right now, but the Crows nearly took advantage there.

Hugo Hall-Kahan had a mark / free from 60-70 out, he kicked over the pack, it nearly bounced through but Judson Clarke got a despairing hand to it a metre or so before it went over the line.

It's a seven-point game in time on in the third term.
